source.version: Undated APA-format author manuscript marked 'UNDER PEER REVIEW'. Retrieval/citation records identify PsyArXiv tbvq2_v1 (doi:10.31234/osf.io/tbvq2_v1), posted 2026-07-03. The later ACM version of record is not the supplied PDF and was not used.
source.supplement_used: Appendix A, Experimental Platform and Paradigm (PDF pp. 33-37, Tables A1-A3); Appendix B, Additional Results (PDF pp. 38-42), both within this PDF.

studies.label: Single experiment: agency instructions with AI access, or no AI, on the Alternative Uses Task

counts_source.quote: external constraints on recruitment duration resulted in a final sample of N = 150.

arms.name: High-Agency
arms.description: Embedded chatbot with instructions to use AI to expand upon their own ideas and generate more creative ones (PDF p. 11).

arms.name: Low-Agency
arms.description: Same chatbot with instructions to let AI's creative power work for them and do the heavy lifting (PDF p. 11).

arms.name: Control (human only)
arms.description: Same AUT without chatbot access, explicitly instructed not to use AI (PDF p. 11).

studies.task: Generate five alternative uses for each of three objects (brick, bubble wrap, frisbee) in a single untimed session with object order counterbalanced (PDF p. 12).

ai_tool.name: gpt-3.5, custom chatbot embedded in Qualtrics through a web application
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 11, Submission Phase; PDF p. 33, Appendix A

preregistration.where: OSF https://osf.io/2d7fe/overview?view_only=c34f80bd046e4c85aafdee3d2c33a74e (PDF p. 10; deviations on PDF p. 14)
preregistration.primary_outcome: Third-party ratings of creativity, originality, and usefulness (H1), and condition-level homogeneity (H2, similarity to the condition-object centroid); PDF p. 9 and PDF pp. 14-16. Clustering outcomes are exploratory (PDF pp. 2, 16).

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Third-party U.S. adults recruited through CloudResearch Connect rated submitted AUT ideas using Table A1's rubric (PDF pp. 10, 13, 34). The evaluators' numeric scale is not explicitly stated. Table A2 analyzes ratings with submitter and object random intercepts.

stats.difference_is: Control (human only) minus Low-Agency (control minus treatment); describes regression.coef, not a separately printed difference

regression.model: Linear mixed-effects model (lme4): condition fixed effect, submitter and object random intercepts, Low-Agency reference. Model-based SE; no robust correction stated. Printed coefficient: Control (human only) minus Low-Agency (control minus treatment).

sources.locator: PDF p. 35, Table A2, Creativity column; Low-Agency reference
PDF p. 35, Table A2, Creativity column, full-model observation count
PDF p. 15, Results, Individual-Level Creativity, model specification
sources.quote: from the fixed effect of condition, with random effects for submitters and objects (bubble wrap, brick, frisbee).

sources.locator: PDF p. 15, Results, conflicting narrative p-value bound
sources.quote: Contrary to our first hypothesis (H1), there were no significant differences in overall idea creativity or originality across the treatment conditions relative to control, ps > .60, as shown in Figure 1.

estimates.notes: Per-protocol analysis excludes AI-arm object trials without chat data and unevaluated ideas (PDF pp. 13-14). n_units is the full-model rating count across all arms, not people or a two-arm count. Model uncertainty accounts for repeated ratings of each submitter through a submitter random intercept, so se_basis is participant when such uncertainty is reported. No observed arm means, arm SDs, or numerical mean-CI endpoints are printed. Figure 1 plots means and intervals; no values are read from it. The reference intercept and random-effect/residual SDs in Table A2 are not entered as observed arm means or arm SDs. The printed coefficient has the reverse orientation to this record. Its sign is preserved and must be reoriented before interpreting the treatment effect. The narrative ps > .60 statement is not identified as the Table A2 coefficient test and does not agree with its coefficient/SE. Table A2 is retained; p_value is null because the table prints no p-value for this row.

sources.locator: PDF p. 17, Results, Homogeneity, exploratory permutation test

sources.locator: PDF p. 17, Results, Homogeneity, permutation procedure
sources.quote: we conducted permutation tests (n = 5,000 permutations) comparing the maximum and minimum condition means for each metric.

estimates.notes: The permutation test compares maximum and minimum condition means, not a separately specified fixed two-arm contrast. The text identifies Control and Low-Agency as driving the observed range. The positive range is stored as test.value and is not converted to a signed treatment-minus-control difference. The test uses 5,000 permutations (PDF p. 17), but the resampling unit is unstated. se_basis is set because uncertainty concerns condition-set metrics and participant-level resampling cannot be verified. Arm levels, SDs, SEs, and CIs are not printed. Figure 3 contains cluster visualizations; no values are read from it. Numbers of people and analyzed sets for this analysis are not printed.

open_items: The supplied PsyArXiv preprint has not been compared with the later ACM proceedings version (doi:10.1145/3803784.3816857).
No number at random assignment is printed. The timing of the initial submitter attention check relative to assignment is unstated (PDF pp. 10-11).

Analyzed total and per-arm participant counts, and pair-specific rating/output counts, are not printed. The final-sample count precedes the described noncompliance exclusions (PDF pp. 13-14). No counts are derived by subtraction or from degrees of freedom.
The sample affected by idea-data-logging exclusions is not named; placement after the evaluator description is insufficient to resolve this (PDF p. 10).
Participant-level and arm-level SDs and observed arm means are not printed. Random-effect and residual SDs in Tables A2 and A3 are not SDs of participant mean outcomes.
Diversity arm levels are missing. Figure 2 plots means and intervals, while Figure 3 shows cluster visualizations; no values are transcribed or reconstructed from intercepts.
The evaluators' numeric rating scale is not explicit; the self-rating scale is not silently applied to evaluator ratings (PDF pp. 12-13, 34).

The Results usefulness coefficient has no named comparator and conflicts with the table and qualitative summaries. The creativity/originality narrative p-value bound also does not agree with the Low-Agency-versus-Control table coefficients and SEs (PDF pp. 15, 17, 35).
The positive High-Agency-versus-Control centroid-similarity t statistic has no stated subtraction order. Its sign is preserved and cannot be assumed to equal treatment minus control (PDF p. 16).
The homogeneity formula uses one minus cosine, while the results, Figure 2, and Table A3 identify cosine similarity. higher_is follows the latter (PDF pp. 15-16, 31, 36).
The centroid input pool, HDBSCAN input pool, clustering embedding model, and permutation resampling unit are not unambiguous (PDF pp. 14-17, 32).
The Discussion asserts a High-Agency-versus-Low-Agency cluster-size-CV difference without a numerical pair-specific result (PDF p. 18).
Remote versus supervised participation is not stated. online_rct is provisional; a supervised session would imply lab_rct (PDF pp. 10-12).
The gpt-3.5 snapshot and its release year are not stated, so ai_tool.year is null (PDF pp. 11, 33).

Both AI arms include agency instructions; neither is uninstructed chatbot use. This matters for subsequent primary-record selection. High-Agency is the proposed configuration for ai_design (PDF pp. 9, 11).
notes: The entire markdown was read in order, including references and both appendices. Every cited PDF page was text-extracted with pymupdf; Tables A2 and A3 column mappings were also checked with text-strategy table extraction. PDF and printed page numbers coincide. No other extraction was consulted. No counts, arm means, contrasts, standardized effects, or SEs were calculated; source quotes retain printed precision. The paper reports N = 150 submitters, but also complete exclusion of 12 High-Agency and 10 Low-Agency participants for noncompliance and removal of AI-arm object trials without chat data (PDF pp. 10, 13-14). Neither randomized nor analyzed counts are filled from the final-sample label. Analyses are per-protocol, with differential post-assignment exclusions. Three submitters failed an initial attention check; the later sentence on attention-check and logging exclusions does not explicitly name the affected sample (PDF p. 10). Low-Agency-versus-Control coefficients retain their printed Control-minus-Low-Agency sign; the reverse orientation is explicit in stats and notes. The gpt-5-mini used to analyze chat logs (PDF pp. 37-39) was not the chatbot supplied to participants. No sample overlap is named in the reconciled screening form.
